requirement_text.REQ-428: Third MOB-4 requirement. Task routes (lib/letflow/routers/tasks.ex): GET /api/v1/tasks/inbox, GET /api/v1/tasks/:id, POST /api/v1/tasks/:id/claim, POST /api/v1/tasks/:id/complete. The task form is resolved through REQ-424's pinned resolver and rendered by REQ-427's form renderer; never the active version. Process-instance renderer: read-only view of GET /api/v1/instances/:id and /api/v1/instances/:id/timeline (lib/letflow/routers/instances.ex) -- status, current step, timeline. No cancel/rebind/advance actions (not in MOB-4). All screens use REQ-426's six-state wrapper; claim/complete errors (409 already claimed, 403, 422) map to its states.

task.description: Verify branch feature/WF02-REQ428-20261001 (git branch --show-current). Implement lib/letflow/design/req428-task-and-instance-renderer.md exactly, in apps/mobile/ only: TaskInboxController/TaskInboxItem (list inbox), TaskDetailController/TaskDetail/claim with TaskClaimOutcome sealed type (claim against POST .../claim, mapping 409 to a distinct 'task no longer available' outcome that triggers an inbox refresh, 403/422 mapped per the design's error table), complete (thin composition over REQ-427's FormRendererController.submit(), posting form values to POST .../complete), task form resolution through apps/mobile/lib/definitions/pinned_form_resolver.dart's resolve() (never looking up the active version), InstanceDetailController with two independent RendererStates for detail and timeline against GET /api/v1/instances/:id and /instances/:id/timeline, with NO cancel/rebind/advance/reconstruct action anywhere in the new code. Every screen routes its errors through the existing six-state RendererState wrapper per the design's §5 table. Do not touch web/ or lib/letflow/ -- if you find a backend/contract gap, STOP and report it to ORCH (do not shim it). Follow apps/mobile/'s existing widget/controller conventions from REQ-426/427 rather than inventing new ones. Design doc's open questions OQ-2 (navigation entry point) and OQ-4 (derive 'current step' from the timeline's most recent non-null node_id entry, no dedicated field exists) are yours to resolve with reasonable judgement consistent with the existing app shell; state what you chose and why in your result.summary. Run, from apps/mobile/: flutter analyze && flutter test, and quote real output -- fix and retry on any failure.
acceptance_criteria: a test lists the inbox from a fake GET /api/v1/tasks/inbox, claims a task (asserting POST /api/v1/tasks/:id/claim), opens it, and completes it (asserting POST /api/v1/tasks/:id/complete with the form values in the body)
a test asserts opening a task pinned to form_version 1 while version 2 is cached renders version 1's fields (through REQ-424's resolver), not version 2's
a test asserts a 409 on claim renders a state telling the user the task is no longer available and refreshes the inbox, not a crash
a test asserts the process-instance screen renders status and timeline entries from fake /instances/:id and /instances/:id/timeline responses and exposes no cancel, rebind or advance action
`cd apps/mobile && flutter analyze && flutter test` pass, real output quoted
No general scripting runtime introduced on-device; no token stored anywhere but OS-secure storage (unchanged by this requirement, but self-review against it per the mobile-dev role file)

result.summary: Implemented lib/letflow/design/req428-task-and-instance-renderer.md in apps/mobile/lib/renderers/task/task.dart and apps/mobile/lib/renderers/process/process.dart: TaskInboxController/TaskInboxItem/TaskStatus, TaskDetail/TaskDetailController, the shared TaskClaimOutcome sealed type + claimTask() (409->TaskClaimNoLongerAvailable, 403->TaskClaimForbidden, network->TaskClaimNetworkUnavailable, other->TaskClaimOtherFailure), task completion as a thin composition over REQ-427's FormRendererController.submit() (no second submit mechanism), and InstanceDetailController with two independent RendererStates (detailState/timelineState) against GET /api/v1/instances/:id and /instances/:id/timeline, with zero cancel/rebind/reconstruct/advance-timer code anywhere (guard-tested). Task form resolution goes exclusively through pinned_form_resolver.dart's resolve() -- TaskDetail.formId/formVersion flow unchanged into FormRendererController's constructor, never an active-version lookup. One implementation judgment call beyond the design doc's literal text: TaskInboxController.client is typed PostCapableHttpGateway, not the bare HttpGateway design section 2.3's prose names -- claim() needs POST capability and ApiClient (the sole production implementation) already satisfies that interface, so this is a client-side interface-typing correction, not a behavior change (documented inline in task.dart). Also made TaskInboxController.claim() AWAIT refreshAfterClaimConflict() (not fire-and-forget) so AC3's 'triggers an inbox refresh' is a deterministic, testable effect of claim()'s own returned Future, not a race. OQ-2 (navigation entry point): left unresolved per the design's own instruction (future screen-wiring/routing code); built TaskDetailScreen/TaskInboxScreen/ProcessInstanceScreen as composable widgets ready for a future go_router route to construct, with TaskDetailScreen taking an optional onClaimConflict callback for the screen-composition layer to wire to an inbox controller's refreshAfterClaimConflict(). OQ-4 (current-step derivation): implemented exactly as the design specifies -- deriveCurrentStepNodeId() in process.dart returns the most recent timeline entry's non-null node_id, shown only for an ACTIVE instance; a terminal instance shows its terminal status instead (no second endpoint read). No backend/contract gap found -- lib/letflow/routers/tasks.ex and instances.ex response shapes matched the design doc's own citations exactly (task_list_item_map/2, task_detail_map/3, instance_map/1, timeline_item_map/1, and rendererStateForError's existing ConflictError->RendererFetchFailure arm, which OQ-3 had flagged as possibly missing but is in fact present in renderer_state.dart as shipped -- no fix needed there). AC5's live-check clause (local docker-compose stack on emulator-5554 with an already-authenticated session) is DEFERRED to UAT-RUNNER: `adb devices` returns an empty device list in this execution context (no Android emulator running) and no mobile build/run harness is configured here; docker compose itself is up (keycloak/postgres both healthy) but there is no emulator to pair it with.
result.next_action: Route to SECURITY-REVIEWER (2c) to check scope -- REQ-428 touches no auth/token/transport code (TaskDetailController/TaskInboxController/InstanceDetailController all delegate exclusively to the existing ApiClient/HttpGateway/PostCapableHttpGateway interfaces, no new Dio/secure-storage/transport-policy code), but per WF-02 every requirement still gets the scope check.
